This R markdown explores individual climate grid cells for MORA.

# 1. Workspace setup

```{r setup}

knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE,  
                      message = FALSE, 
                      warning = FALSE, 
                      eval = TRUE)

# This Rmd lives in Reports/, but all paths (data/, src/, setup.R) are relative
# to the project root. root.dir applies from the next chunk on; chdir = TRUE
# lets setup.R find src/ while this chunk still runs from Reports/.
knitr::opts_knit$set(root.dir = here::here())

# Load functions after park files in case functions were updated since last save.
source(here::here("setup.R"), chdir = TRUE)
library(rnoaa)

# Set mapview basemap options
mapviewOptions(fgb = FALSE, 
               georaster = FALSE, 
               basemaps = c("Esri.WorldTopoMap",
                            "Esri.WorldImagery"))

# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Color system (validated for WCAG contrast + colorblind-safe separation)
#
# The core categorical hues below were checked with an OKLCH-based
# validator against: lightness band, chroma floor, CVD separation
# (protanopia/deuteranopia simulation), a normal-vision separation floor,
# and contrast vs. a white page (relevant since this report renders as a
# static Word document - figures are flat images, not interactive).
#
# Two documented, deliberate exceptions to the validator's defaults:
#   1. The neutral "Historical" gray (#595959) reads slightly below the
#      validator's chroma floor - expected and accepted for a pure neutral
#      used in a structural/reference role (a baseline period, not a
#      scenario), same treatment the validator itself allows for
#      diverging-palette midpoints. Its old value (gray80) was replaced
#      because gray80 fails contrast against a white page outright (WCAG
#      violation, and nearly invisible in a printed/grayscale copy).
#   2. "Projected" orange (#a1631f) was validated against the other three
#      core colors in "adjacent" mode (the check that matches how these
#      colors are actually used here - as neighbors in a line/bar/ribbon
#      legend), not the stricter "any two colors simultaneously visible"
#      mode meant for scatter/choropleth work. Orange and the CF red never
#      appear together in the same chart in this report, so the stricter
#      check isn't the relevant one for this palette's actual use.
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------

# Non CF colors (still under review - not yet reconciled to the validated
# system below; pal$orange and pal$darkblue ARE now part of the validated
# system, see note beside plot_colors)
pal <- list(
  black = "black", 
  gold = "#dca237", 
  lightblue = "#6eb2e4", 
  teal = "#459a74", 
  yellow = "#eee461", 
  darkblue = "#1b6ca8",   # validated - now shared with nps_pal$blue / "Snowy Wet"
  orange = "#a1631f",     # validated "Projected" - replaces the old #c66426
  pink = "#c07da5",
  lightpink = "#ECD8E4"
)

# Named Colors for general 2 tone cf
# grey/lightgrey below are not yet reconciled to the validated system
# (pending the full palette sweep); blue/red are validated core colors.
nps_pal <-list(blue = "#1b6ca8",   # validated
               red = "#b02a24",    # validated
               grey = "#a9a9a9", 
               lightgrey = "#dcdcdc")


# Colors for CF plots - validated core categorical palette.
# "Observed" stays pure black (max contrast, deliberately distinct from
# "Historical" by lightness alone since both are neutral/structural roles
# rather than scenario hues).
plot_colors = c("Less Snowy Dry" = nps_pal$red, 
                "Snowy Wet" = nps_pal$blue,  
                "Observed" = "black", 
                "Historical" = "#595959")

# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Shared plot theme
#
# One theme function used across figures for a consistent, professional
# look: legible text sizing, a restrained gridline, legend on the bottom
# (keeps the plot area wide for the Word-doc page), and clean panel
# borders instead of a boxed-in look.
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
theme_wsva <- function(base_size = 11, legend = "bottom") {
  theme_minimal(base_size = base_size) +
    theme(
      plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = rel(1.1), margin = margin(b = 4)),
      plot.subtitle = element_text(color = "gray30", size = rel(0.95), margin = margin(b = 8)),
      plot.caption = element_text(color = "gray40", size = rel(0.75), hjust = 0),
      axis.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = rel(0.95)),
      axis.text = element_text(color = "gray20"),
      panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
      panel.grid.major = element_line(color = "gray90", linewidth = 0.3),
      strip.text = element_text(face = "bold", size = rel(0.95)),
      strip.background = element_rect(fill = "gray95", color = NA),
      legend.position = legend,
      legend.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = rel(0.9)),
      legend.text = element_text(size = rel(0.9))
    )
}

# Create output directories
dir.create("data/park/MORA/Figs", showWarnings = FALSE, recursive = TRUE)
dir.create("data/park/MORA/Tables", showWarnings = FALSE, recursive = TRUE)


# Define conversions
gal_to_cf <- 0.133681
cf_to_gal <- 1/gal_to_cf

# Define time periods
# BOTH ends of each window are INCLUSIVE: historical baseline = 1980-2012
# (1979 is the WBM spin-up year and is excluded); future = 2035-2064 (ends just
# before 2065-01-01). Always filter with year >= x[1] & year <= x[2].
hist_yrs <- c(1980, 2012)
fut_yrs <- c(2035, 2064)

# Pick CRS for project
crs_use <- "EPSG:5070"

```

# 1b. Analysis functions

Helper functions for this report are defined here, per project convention.

Define park using 4-digit NPS Unit Code. Codes for all parks can be found at: 
<https://www.nps.gov/aboutus/foia/upload/NPS-Unit-List.xlsx>.

Download the park boundary from the NPS IRMA DataStore as an {sf} object.

```{r park_dat}

park <- "MORA"

# Get park geometry and metadata
park_boundary <- getParkBoundary(park = park)
state <- park_boundary$STATE

park_boundary <- st_transform(park_boundary,
                              crs_use)

mapview(park_boundary,
        col.regions = "seagreen")

```

# 2. Water supplies

A water supply system database was created for this project using various
NPS and public databases. The database contains a row for each water supply
system and source of water (e.g., individual wells, diversions, and springs)
associated with each supply. Here, we focus on the Paradise water supply
system per NPS WRD direction.

```{r}

# Import database and convert to spatial (sf) object
wsd <- get_wsd() %>%
  dplyr::filter(park_unit == park) %>%
  st_transform(., crs_use) %>%
  dplyr::filter(grepl("Paradise", water_system_name)) %>%
  st_transform(., crs_use)

```

# 3. Load supplementary datasets

## - Watersheds

Get watershed associated with the water supply point and other watersheds that 
overlap the park.

#### - Surface Water

We delineated contributing watersheds for the current Edith Creek intake, the
proposed downstream intake, and the Paradise Valley groundwater-fed area below,
so that available water volumes can be compared across all three candidate
systems on a common basis (modeled runoff x catchment area).

#### - Current System (Edith) 

Load watersheds for the current system on Edith Creek, downstream system on Edith Creek, and Paradise Valley outlet.

```{r edith_watersheds}


system_watershed <-  st_read('data/park/MORA/edithcreek_watershed.gpkg') %>%
  st_transform(crs_use)

system_watershed_ft2 <- st_area(system_watershed) %>% 
  set_units(ft^2) %>%
  as.numeric()

# Potential new intake - downstream of current intake, to increase contributing area

potential_intake <- st_read('data/park/MORA/From_WRD/MORA_paradise_potential_intake.kml')


down_edith_creek_watershed <- st_read('./data/park/MORA/downstream_edithcreek/downstream_edithcreek_watershed.gpkg') %>%
  st_transform(crs_use)

down_edith_ft2 <- down_edith_creek_watershed %>%
  st_area() %>% 
  set_units(ft^2) %>%
  as.numeric()

paradise_river_watershed <- 
  st_read('./data/park/MORA/paradise_river/paradise_river_watershed.gpkg') %>%

paradise_watershed_ft2 <- paradise_river_watershed %>%

st_area(paradise_river_watershed) %>%
```

Pull in NOAA weather stations near the park

```{r}

# Get weather data for all stations (depending on dates and how many stations this can take a while)
# noaa <- getNOAA(park_boundary, park_boundary$UNIT_CODE) %>%
#   st_transform(crs_use)

# saveRDS(noaa, "data/park/MORA/MORA_noaa.rds")
noaa <- readRDS("data/park/MORA/MORA_noaa.rds")

# Get list of stations with geospatial attributes
stations <- noaa %>%
  group_by(name) %>%
  slice(1) %>%
  ungroup()

# Tidy data
weather_data <- noaa %>%
  dplyr::select(id, 
                name, 
                date, 
                prcp, 
                snow, 
                snwd, 
                tmax, 
                tmin, 
                tobs,
                wesd) %>%
  # info stored as data * 10 for these params... so reconvert:
  dplyr::mutate_at(c("tmax", "tmin", "prcp", "wesd"), function(x) {x * 0.10}) %>%
  # convert from mm to inches
  dplyr::mutate_at(c("snow","snwd", "prcp", "wesd"), function(x) {x * 0.0393701}) %>%
  # convert from Celsius to Fahrenheit
  dplyr::mutate_at(c("tmax","tmin"), function(x) {(9/5) * x + 32})

unique(weather_data$id)

mapview(weather_data) +
  mapview(system_watershed,
          col.region = 'pink')

# Remove raw weather data and clear mem
rm(noaa)
gc()


```

### -- SNOTEL

Read in nearby SNOTEL sites and download and compare data to weather station.

Started with 20 km distance for SNOTEL. The sites that are farther away will
likely be removed before analysis because they are not representative of the 
system catchment.

```{r snotel}

# saveRDS(snotel_hourly, "data/park/MORA/snotel_hourly.rds")

snotel_daily <- readRDS("data/park/MORA/snotel_daily.rds")
snotel_hourly <- readRDS("data/park/MORA/snotel_hourly.rds")

# Get SNOTEL locations
# Coordinates come in as WGS84 lon/lat, so project to albers
snotel_sites <- snotel_daily %>%
  group_by(site) %>%
  dplyr::slice(1) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  st_as_sf(coords = c("longitude", "latitude"), crs = 4326) %>%
  st_transform(crs_use)

# Compare NOAA and SNOTEL stations
mapview(park_boundary, 
        col.regions = "seagreen") +
  mapview(snotel_sites,
          col.regions= 'purple') +
  mapview(system_watershed,
    col.regions = "dodgerblue",
    alpha.regions = 0.5
  )

snotel_daily_tidy <- snotel_daily %>%
  dplyr::select(date, 
                name, 
                value, 
                sensor_id, 
                water_year) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(date = as_date(date),
                value = as.numeric(value)) %>%
  arrange(date) %>%
  distinct(date, 
           name, 
           sensor_id, 
           .keep_all = TRUE) %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = sensor_id, 
              values_from = value) %>%
  clean_names() %>%
  # --- Calculate Incremental Daily Precipitation ---
  group_by(name) %>%
  arrange(date, .by_group = TRUE) %>%
  mutate(
    # Simple lag difference
    precip_diff = prec_i - lag(prec_i),
    
    # Handle Water Year reset (Oct 1) & initial day:
    # If it's the first record or prec_i dropped (reset), set to current prec_i
    daily_precip = case_when(
      is.na(precip_diff) ~ prec_i,
      precip_diff < 0    ~ prec_i,  # Handles WY reset or sensor recalibration
      TRUE               ~ precip_diff
    )
  ) %>%
  dplyr::select(-precip_diff) %>%
  ungroup()

# Again remove unused data
rm(snotel_daily)
gc()

# Look at temporal overlap
ggplot(snotel_daily_tidy, 
       aes(x = date, 
           y = name, 
           color = name)) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 2) +
  theme_wsva() +
  labs(x = "", 
       y = "", 
       color = "Station Name") +
  theme(legend.position = "none") +
  ggtitle('Temporal overlap')

# Prep snotel hourly data
  snotel_hourly <- snotel_hourly %>%
    # the date & time columns = the local time at MORA
    # & lines up w/ snotel site
    mutate(datetime = ymd_hm(paste(date, time))) %>%
    select(datetime,
           name,
           water_year,
           water_day,
           value,
           depth,
           sensor_id) %>%

         depth = as.numeric(depth))
```

Based on the preliminary assessment above, only the following stations will be
considered.
- Cayuse Pass (SNOTEL)

- Rainier Paradise RS (NWS COOP)

A note on the Paradise SNOTEL, this is in a forested area at a lower elevation.
The snow persistence isn't that different (~93%), but will need to be careful
because there will be more interception here, less incoming shortwave radiation,
more transpiration, etc.

# 5. Climate and Water Balance

## - GCM Selection

Climate futures were previously compiled for park and Koppen centroids. This data was used to select which of the CMIP5 climate models to use to represent "hot dry" and "warm wet" scenarios. Here, we read in the pre-determined gcm selections.

We load these in, but at Mount Rainier, the greatest change in runoff (+ and -) corresponds to precipitation and specifically snow changes

```{r}

# Read in selected "Hot dry" "Warm Wet" climate futures
centroid_cfs <- data.table::fread('data/parkwide_gcms.csv') %>%
  dplyr::filter(park %in% {{park}},
                CF %in% c("Warm Wet", "Hot Dry")) %>%
  distinct(GCM, .keep_all = TRUE)

# If there is more than one model selection for a CF scenario, grab the more divergent.
if (nrow(centroid_cfs) > 2) {
  if (nrow(centroid_cfs %>% dplyr::filter(CF == "Hot Dry")) > 1) {
    centroid_cfs <- centroid_cfs %>%
      group_by(CF) %>%
      slice_min(delta_pr)
  }
  if ((nrow(centroid_cfs %>% dplyr::filter(CF == "Warm Wet")) > 1) ) {
    centroid_cfs <- centroid_cfs %>%
      group_by(CF) %>%
      slice_max(delta_pr)
  }
}

# Read in all available gcms
all_cfs <-
  read_delim( "https://raw.githubusercontent.com/rossyndicate/CCRP_automated_climate_futures/master/data/general/GCM_skill_by_region.txt" ) %>%
  dplyr::filter(Region == "PWR") %>% #,
                #Rank < 19) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(GCM = ifelse(GCM == "HadGEM2-ES.", "HadGEM2-ES365.", GCM),
                GCM = ifelse(GCM == "HadGEM2-CC.", "HadGEM2-CC365.", GCM)) %>%
  tidyr::crossing(data.table(RCP = c("rcp45","rcp85"))) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(GCM = paste0(GCM,RCP)) %>% 
  dplyr::mutate(Skill = ifelse(Rank > 18, "Low Skill", "High Skill"))
  

# Workspace cleanup: these are no longer used after this point.
rm(wbm_gcms)
gc()
```

```{r}
clim_fut <- readRDS("data/park/MORA/clim_fut_extra.rds") %>%
  mutate(x = round(x,6),
         y = round(y,6)) 

# 2. Helper function: find the nearest historical coordinate for each future coordinate using simple absolute difference
get_nearest <- function(fut_vec, hist_vec) {
  u_fut  <- unique(fut_vec)
  u_hist <- unique(hist_vec)
  # For each unique future value, pick the historical value with min absolute difference
  matched_hist <- u_hist[sapply(u_fut, function(v) which.min(abs(u_hist - v)))]
  # Map back to full vector
  matched_hist[match(fut_vec, u_fut)]
}

# 3. Apply substitution directly to clim_fut
clim_fut <- clim_fut %>%
  mutate(
    x = get_nearest(x, clim_hist$x),
    y = get_nearest(y, clim_hist$y)
  )


clim_fut_sf <- clim_fut %>%
  distinct(x, y) %>%
  sf::st_as_sf(coords = c("x", "y"), crs = 4326)

# quick view of the 6 points/grids
mapview(aoi_gridmet_grid) +
mapview(clim_pts) +
mapview(clim_fut_sf) + 
  mapview(system_watershed)


# Workspace cleanup: these are no longer used after this point.
rm(clim_fut_sf)
gc()
```

## - Run WBM all grids

We use the NPS water balance model (WBM) to calculate water budget components. 
The model requires temperature and precipitation inputs, which we've now 
downloaded for historical and projected periods. The water balance model is 
adapted from code base developed in NPS's {WaterBalance} package 
(<https://github.com/CCRP-Adaptation/WaterBalance>).

For our report, we ran the NPS water balance model (WBM) for each GridMET point
in the source area. The average soil moisture capacity, elevation, slope, and 
aspect are used as inputs for each model run. We then aggregate the values to 
the weighted mean for the recharge area, returning a spatially averaged daily 
value. We are running the historical and future datasets separately, but use 
final conditions from the historical as the starting conditions for the future.

```{r wbm_run_all_grids}
  left_join(all_cfs, by = "GCM") %>%
  dplyr::mutate(runoff_gal_edith_wbm = (runoff_in_wbm / 12) * system_watershed_ft2 * cf_to_gal,
                runoff_gal_down_edith_wbm = (runoff_in_wbm/12) * down_edith_ft2 * cf_to_gal,
                runoff_gal_paradise_wbm = (runoff_in_wbm/12) * paradise_watershed_ft2 * cf_to_gal)

```

Look at temp, precip, and runoff across the grids to select pixels to use since 
in this case we are looking at many pixels not just pixels that the watershed is 
within.

```{r pick pixels, fig.width=14, fig.height=10}

wbm_xy_stats <- wbm_all %>%
  dplyr::mutate(
    year       = year(date),
    stat_period = ifelse(year >= hist_yrs[1] & year <= hist_yrs[2], "Baseline",
                  ifelse(year >= fut_yrs[1] & year <= fut_yrs[2], "Future", "Other"))
  ) %>%
  dplyr::filter(stat_period != "Other") %>%
  dplyr::select(GCM, stat_period, x, y, Skill, precip_in_wbm, tmean_C, runoff_in_wbm, pet_in_wbm) %>%
  dplyr::group_by(GCM, stat_period, Skill, x, y) %>%
  dplyr::summarize(
    mean_precip_in          = mean(precip_in_wbm),
    mean_tmean_C            = mean(tmean_C),
    mean_runoff_in          = mean(runoff_in_wbm),
    median_runoff_in        = quantile(runoff_in_wbm, 0.75),
    sd_runoff_in            = sd(runoff_in_wbm),
    cv_runoff_in            = sd(runoff_in_wbm) / mean(runoff_in_wbm),
    iqr_runoff_in           = as.numeric(quantile(runoff_in_wbm, 0.75)) -
                              as.numeric(quantile(runoff_in_wbm, 0.25)),
    q90_q10_runoff_in       = as.numeric(quantile(runoff_in_wbm, 0.9)) -
                              as.numeric(quantile(runoff_in_wbm, 0.1)),
    peak_runoff_in          = max(runoff_in_wbm),
    mean_precip_minus_pet_in = mean(precip_in_wbm - pet_in_wbm),
    fract_zero_runoff       = sum(runoff_in_wbm == 0) / n(),
    .groups = "keep"
  )

baseline_xy <- wbm_xy_stats %>%
  dplyr::filter(stat_period == "Baseline") %>%
  rename_with(~ paste0(.x, "_baseline"),
              all_of(c("mean_precip_in", "mean_tmean_C", "mean_runoff_in",
                        "median_runoff_in", "sd_runoff_in", "cv_runoff_in",
                        "iqr_runoff_in", "q90_q10_runoff_in", "peak_runoff_in",
                        "mean_precip_minus_pet_in", "fract_zero_runoff"))) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  dplyr::select(-stat_period)

future_xy <- wbm_xy_stats %>%
  dplyr::filter(stat_period != "Baseline") %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  dplyr::select(-stat_period)

future_differentials_xy <- future_xy %>%
  dplyr::ungroup() %>%
  left_join(baseline_xy %>% dplyr::ungroup() %>% dplyr::select(-c(GCM, Skill)),
            by = c("x", "y")) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(
    delta_precip_in    = mean_precip_in - mean_precip_in_baseline,
    delta_tmean_C      = mean_tmean_C   - mean_tmean_C_baseline,
    delta_runoff_in    = 365.25 * (mean_runoff_in - mean_runoff_in_baseline),
    delta_runoff_in_sd = sd_runoff_in   - sd_runoff_in_baseline) 

future_differentials_xy_sf <- future_differentials_xy %>%
  dplyr::ungroup() %>%
  st_as_sf(coords = c("x", "y"), crs = 4326, remove = FALSE)

# transform the system_watereshed into 4326 to match above
# also simplify watershed since it's vertex heavy due to being
# lidar-derived
watershed <- system_watershed %>% 
  st_transform(., st_crs(future_differentials_xy_sf)) %>%
  st_simplify(dTolerance = 10)

# --- Runoff delta raster (stars) ---
runoff_raster <- future_differentials_xy %>%
  dplyr::mutate(x = round(x, 4), y = round(y, 4)) %>%
  dplyr::select(x, y, GCM, delta_runoff_in) %>%
  st_as_stars(dims = c("x", "y", "GCM"), dx = 4000, dy = 4000) 

ggplot() +
  geom_stars(data = runoff_raster) +
  geom_sf(data = watershed, fill = NA, color = "black", linewidth = 0.5) +
  facet_wrap(~GCM, ncol = 8) +
  scale_fill_distiller(palette = "RdBu", name = "Delta Runoff (in)",
                       direction = 1, na.value = "transparent") +
  theme_wsva() +
  labs(title = "30-Year Runoff Delta by GCM") +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom",
        axis.text = element_blank(), axis.ticks = element_blank())

ggsave("data/park/MORA/Figs/delta_runoff_grid.jpg", dpi = 600)

# --- Temp delta raster (stars) ---
tmean_raster <- future_differentials_xy %>%
  dplyr::mutate(x = round(x, 4), y = round(y, 4)) %>%
  dplyr::select(x, y, GCM, delta_tmean_C) %>%
  st_as_stars(dims = c("x", "y", "GCM"), dx = 4000, dy = 4000)

ggplot() +
  geom_stars(data = tmean_raster) +
  geom_sf(data = watershed, fill = NA, color = "black", linewidth = 0.5) +
  facet_wrap(~GCM, ncol = 8) +
  scale_fill_distiller(palette = "OrRd", name = "Delta Temp (°C)",
                       direction = 1, na.value = "transparent") +
  theme_wsva() +
  labs(title = "30-Year Temp Delta by GCM") +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom",
        axis.text = element_blank(), axis.ticks = element_blank())

ggsave("data/park/MORA/Figs/delta_tmean_grid.jpg", dpi = 600)

# --- Precip delta raster (stars) ---
precip_raster <- future_differentials_xy %>%
  dplyr::mutate(x = round(x, 4), y = round(y, 4)) %>%
  dplyr::select(x, y, GCM, delta_precip_in) %>%
  st_as_stars(dims = c("x", "y", "GCM"), dx = 4000, dy = 4000)

ggplot() +
  geom_stars(data = precip_raster) +
  geom_sf(data = watershed, fill = NA, color = "black", linewidth = 0.5) +
  facet_wrap(~GCM, ncol = 8) +
  scale_fill_distiller(palette = "BrBG", name = "Delta Precip (in)",
                       direction = 1, na.value = "transparent") +
  theme_wsva() +
  labs(title = "30-Year Precip Delta by GCM") +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom",
        axis.text = element_blank(), axis.ticks = element_blank())

ggsave("data/park/MORA/Figs/delta_precip_grid.jpg", dpi = 600)
```

```{r select_specific_climate_cells}
# get distinct x,y points
# we want the top 3 pts based on above
# I also looked at snow persistence and elevation and the top 2 outer points
# are most similar to the point w/in the catchment
select_clim_pts <- clim_pts %>%
  filter(y > 46.81) %>%  # just used the y coords to filter for the top 3
  filter(x < -121.7) # remove the eastern grid

mapview(aoi_gridmet_grid) + mapview(select_clim_pts)

clim_hist <- clim_hist %>%
  filter(y > 46.81) %>%  # just used the y coords to filter for the top 3
  filter(x < -121.7)

clim_fut <- clim_fut %>%
  filter(y > 46.81) %>%  # just used the y coords to filter for the top 3
  filter(x < -121.7)



# Workspace cleanup: these are no longer used after this point.
rm(baseline_xy, clim_pts, future_differentials_xy, future_differentials_xy_sf, future_xy, precip_raster, runoff_raster, tmean_raster, wbm_xy_stats)
gc()
```

I evaluated the climate grid cells to the west, east, and south of the watershed
(6 total). The 3 southern grids were removed as immediately after evaluating 
elevation and land cover. Leaving the grid the watershed is within and one to 
the west and east. Further evaluation showed that the eastern cell,
while tracking cumulative precipitation similarly to the other two cells and 
the Paradise SNOTEL station, consistently produced much lower cumulative SWE. 
Investigating the cause, I found this cell sits at a lower elevation than the 
other two — so despite comparable precipitation totals, a greater amount of 
precip falls as rain rather than snow, driving the divergence in cumulative SWE. 
Based on this, I retained only two grid cells for the analysis: the cell 
containing the watershed and the cell to the west.

```{r}
# Combine hist and fut wbm. All indicates still separate grid cells
wbm_all <- hist_wbm %>%
  #dplyr::select(-c(, discharge_cfs, runoff_cfs_wbm)) %>%
  bind_rows(fut_wbm) %>%
  as.data.table() %>%
  left_join(all_cfs, by = "GCM") %>%
  dplyr::mutate(runoff_gal_edith_wbm = (runoff_in_wbm / 12) * system_watershed_ft2 * cf_to_gal,
                runoff_gal_down_edith_wbm = (runoff_in_wbm/12) * down_edith_ft2 * cf_to_gal,
                runoff_gal_paradise_wbm = (runoff_in_wbm/12) * paradise_watershed_ft2 * cf_to_gal)
```

## - Hock Calibration

Compare simulated snowpack from the historical (GridMET-driven) WBM run against
observed SNOTEL SWE at Paradise, to assess how well the current `hock_coef`
(set in the `wbm_run` chunk above) reproduces observed snow accumulation/melt
timing and magnitude. Note the SNOTEL station is a single point at a lower,
forested elevation, while the WBM grid cells span the full AOI elevation range,
so this is an approximate calibration, not an exact match.

```{r hock_calibration}

hist_wbm_snow <- wbm_all %>%
  dplyr::filter(GCM == "GridMET") %>%
  dplyr::select(date, x, y, snowpack_in_wbm) %>%
   filter(y > 46.81) %>%  # just used the y coords to filter for the top 3
  filter(x < -121.7)
  

# Grid-cell mean snowpack across all AOI pixels, per day
hist_wbm_mean <- hist_wbm_snow %>%
#  dplyr::filter(x > -121.7660,
#                y > 46.7751) %>%
  dplyr::group_by(date) %>%
  dplyr::summarize(mean_snowpack = mean(snowpack_in_wbm, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop")

# Observed SNOTEL SWE at Paradise
snotel_paradise <- snotel_daily_tidy %>%
  dplyr::filter(name == "Paradise") %>%
  dplyr::select(date, swe_in)

# --- Quantitative fit, across the full period of overlap ---
hock_compare <- snotel_paradise %>%
  dplyr::inner_join(hist_wbm_mean, by = "date") %>%
  tidyr::drop_na(swe_in, mean_snowpack)

rmse_val <- Metrics::rmse(hock_compare$swe_in, hock_compare$mean_snowpack)

# Nash-Sutcliffe Efficiency (1 = perfect fit, 0 = no better than the observed
# mean, <0 = worse than the observed mean). Hand-computed since hydroGOF isn't
# in setup.R - flag if you'd rather add that package and use NSE() directly.
nse_val <- 1 - sum((hock_compare$swe_in - hock_compare$mean_snowpack)^2) /
  sum((hock_compare$swe_in - mean(hock_compare$swe_in))^2)

message("Hock coef: ", hock_coef,
       " | RMSE: ", round(rmse_val, 2), " in",
       " | NSE: ", round(nse_val, 3))

# Collect model fit statistics so they are saved to a table (written in the
# run-methods chunk), not only printed to the console.
fit_stats <- tibble::tibble(
  model = "Hock snowmelt calibration (WBM vs. Paradise SNOTEL SWE)",
  statistic = c("hock_coef", "RMSE (in)", "NSE", "overlap_start", "overlap_end"),
  value = c(as.character(hock_coef), signif(rmse_val, 4), signif(nse_val, 4),
            as.character(min(hock_compare$date)), as.character(max(hock_compare$date))))

# --- Visual check for one selected water year ---
# calc_water_year() is sourced from src/calc_water_year.R via setup.R
calibration_water_year <- 2020

hist_wbm_mean_wy <- hist_wbm_mean %>%
  dplyr::mutate(water_year = calc_water_year(date)) %>%
  dplyr::filter(water_year == calibration_water_year)

ggplot(hist_wbm_mean_wy %>%
    dplyr::left_join(snotel_paradise, by = "date"),
  aes(x = date)
) +
  geom_line(data = hist_wbm_snow %>% 
                   dplyr::mutate(water_year = calc_water_year(date),
                                 coord = paste0(x, ", ", y)) %>%
                   dplyr::filter(water_year == calibration_water_year), 
  aes(y = snowpack_in_wbm, group = coord, color = "WBM GRID")) +
  geom_line(aes(y = mean_snowpack, color = "WBM MEAN"), linewidth = 1) +
  geom_line(aes(y = swe_in, color = "SNOTEL"), linewidth = 1) +
  labs(x = "", y = "Snowpack (in)",
       title = paste0("Water Year ", calibration_water_year,
                      " | Hock Coef: ", hock_coef, " | Overall NSE: ", round(nse_val, 2))) +
  theme_wsva() +
  scale_color_manual("", values = c("WBM GRID" = "#1b6ca8", "WBM MEAN" = "black", "SNOTEL" = "#b02a24")) +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom")

ggsave(paste0("data/park/MORA/Figs/Hock_", hock_coef, "_WY", calibration_water_year, ".jpg"),
      width = 5, height = 4, dpi = 600)


# Workspace cleanup: these are no longer used after this point.
rm(hist_wbm_mean, hist_wbm_mean_wy, hist_wbm_snowpack, hist_wbm_snowpack_wy, hock_coef, hock_compare, nse_val, rmse_val, snotel_paradise)
gc()
```

To calibrate, adjust `hock_coef` in the `wbm_run` chunk above, rerun the historical
WBM (and this section), and compare RMSE/NSE across attempts - higher NSE and
lower RMSE indicate a better match to observed SNOTEL SWE.

## - Cumulative Precip Check

Same comparison as above, but for cumulative precipitation instead of snowpack -
a quick sanity check on the precip forcing driving the WBM. SNOTEL's PREC.I is
already reported as water-year-to-date cumulative, so only the WBM side needs
a `cumsum()`.

```{r cumulative_precip}

# Historical (GridMET-driven) WBM precip, per pixel, cumulative within the
# selected water year
hist_wbm_precip_wy <- wbm_all %>%
  dplyr::filter(GCM == "GridMET") %>%
  dplyr::select(date, x, y, precip_in_wbm) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(water_year = calc_water_year(date)) %>%
  dplyr::filter(water_year == calibration_water_year) %>%
  dplyr::arrange(x, y, date) %>%
  dplyr::group_by(x, y) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(cum_precip_in_wbm = cumsum(precip_in_wbm)) %>%
  dplyr::ungroup()

# Grid-cell mean cumulative precip across all AOI pixels, per day
hist_wbm_precip_mean_wy <- hist_wbm_precip_wy %>%
  dplyr::group_by(date) %>%
  dplyr::summarize(mean_cum_precip = mean(cum_precip_in_wbm, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop")

# Observed cumulative SNOTEL precip at Paradise (PREC.I is already WY-cumulative)
snotel_precip_paradise_wy <- snotel_daily_tidy %>%
  dplyr::filter(name == "Paradise", water_year == calibration_water_year) %>%
  dplyr::select(date, precip_in)

ggplot(
  hist_wbm_precip_wy %>%
    dplyr::left_join(snotel_precip_paradise_wy, by = "date"),
  aes(x = date)
) +
  geom_line(aes(y = cum_precip_in_wbm, color = "WBM GRID", group = paste0(x, y)), linewidth = 1) +
  geom_line(data = hist_wbm_precip_mean_wy,
            aes(y = mean_cum_precip, color = "WBM MEAN"), linewidth = 1) +
  geom_line(aes(y = precip_in, color = "SNOTEL"), linewidth = 1) +
  labs(x = "", y = "Cumulative Precip (in)",
       title = paste0("Water Year ", calibration_water_year, " - Cumulative Precip")) +
  theme_wsva() +
  scale_color_manual("", values = c("WBM GRID" = "#1b6ca8", "WBM MEAN" = "black", "SNOTEL" = "#b02a24")) +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom")

ggsave(paste0("data/park/MORA/Figs/CumulativePrecip_WY", calibration_water_year, ".jpg"),
      width = 7, height = 4, dpi = 600)


# Workspace cleanup: these are no longer used after this point.
rm(calibration_water_year, hist_wbm_precip_mean_wy, hist_wbm_precip_wy, snotel_precip_paradise_wy)
gc()
```
